summary: The numerical and convex-geometric argument is correct under the apparent intended meanings, but the supplied candidate is not self-contained enough for stateless verification: its two essential notions are undefined.
gaps: The functions F_{i,q} are never defined, and no predecessor fact or external source defines them. The proof treats F_{i,q}(r) as the Euclidean area of A_i intersected with the closed halfplane {w:q dot w <= r}; without that definition, the values F_{1,q}(2)=1 and F_{2,q}(5)=1/4, and hence the claimed obstruction, cannot be verified from the supplied material.

The phrase 'compatible with the locked problem' is not defined in the candidate or in any accepted predecessor fact. The proof establishes that the three integer-height sections are A_0, A_1, and A_2, but there is no supplied definition showing that this is exactly the full compatibility requirement.
repair_hints: State the definition of F_{i,q} explicitly and specify that the cap uses the closed halfplane.
State the locked problem's compatibility condition in the candidate and check each of its clauses; if compatibility means exactly equality of the integer-height sections, say so.
